title: In the Father's bosom and in His mother's arms; closing doxology

edition.locus: Vossius 1684 Opera omnia, Latin column, In annuntiationem Sermo I, printed p. 14, col. D, to p. 15, col. A (PDF pp. 38-39)

source_text: Qui occultorum dispensationis mysteriorum omnem implevit providentiam ac dispositionem in caelo in sinu Patris, et in spelunca in ulnis matris, in praesepio requievit. Chori Angelici circumcingebant eum, in caelo gloriam concinentes, et in terra pacem adnuntiantes. In caelo a dextris Patris sedebat; et in praesepio, ut super Cherubim requiescebat. Thronus revera et hic erat Cherubicus; Thronus regalis; sanctus sanctorum; solus super terram gloriosus; sanctis sanctior; in quo requievit Christus Deus noster. Cui gloria, honor, et imperium, cum immaculatissimo Patre, et sanctissimo ac vivifico Spiritu: nunc et semper, et in saecula saeculorum, Amen.
pass_a_gloss: Who, of the hidden mysteries of the dispensation (occulta dispensationis mysteria) all the providence (providentia) and arrangement (dispositio) fulfilled (implevit), in heaven in the bosom of the Father (in sinu Patris), and in the cave (spelunca) in the arms of the mother (in ulnis matris), in the manger rested (requievit). Angelic choirs surrounded (circumcingebant) Him, in heaven glory (gloria) singing together (concinentes), and on earth peace (pax) announcing (adnuntiantes). In heaven at the right hand of the Father (a dextris Patris) He was sitting (sedebat); and in the manger, as above the Cherubim (super Cherubim), He was resting (requiescebat). Truly (revera) this also was a Cherubic throne (thronus Cherubicus); a royal throne (thronus regalis); holy of holies (sanctus sanctorum); alone on earth glorious (gloriosus); holier than the holy (sanctis sanctior); in which rested Christ our God. To whom glory (gloria), honor (honor), and dominion (imperium), with the most immaculate Father (immaculatissimus Pater), and the most holy and life-giving Spirit (vivificus Spiritus): now and always, and to the ages of ages (in saecula saeculorum), Amen.

pass_b_english: He who carried out the whole providence and ordering of the hidden mysteries of the dispensation, in heaven in the bosom of the Father and in the cave in His mother's arms, rested in the manger. Choirs of angels surrounded Him, singing glory in heaven and announcing peace on earth (Luke 2:13-14). In heaven He sat at the right hand of the Father; and in the manger He rested as upon the cherubim. Truly this too was a throne of the cherubim, a royal throne: the holy of holies, alone glorious upon earth, holier than the holy, in which Christ our God rested.
To Him be glory, honor, and dominion, with the all-pure Father and the most holy and life-giving Spirit, now and always, and to the ages of ages. Amen.
notes: 'gloriam ... pacem' alludes to the angels' song in Luke 2:13-14; cited. 'a dextris Patris sedebat' is stock creedal language (compare Psalm 110:1; Hebrews 1:3) and 'super Cherubim' recalls Psalm 80:1, cited in section 17; neither cited again here. 'in sinu Patris' recalls John 1:18, cited in section 13. The sentence 'Qui ... implevit ... in praesepio requievit' has two verbs on one relative; rendered as one sentence with 'He who carried out ... rested in the manger', the two 'in heaven ... in the cave' phrases standing between them as in the Latin. 'Thronus ... et hic erat' taken with hic as the pronoun ('this too was a throne'); 'here too' would also fit. 'immaculatissimo Patre' rendered 'the all-pure Father'. 'in spelunca' (the cave of the Nativity) is the author's, not Luke's. '[s]uper' and '[i]n quo' as supplied in the source row; the margin variant 'al. occulto dispensationis mysterio' not adopted.
source_notes: PDF p. 38 = printed p. 14, col. D, to PDF p. 39 = printed p. 15, col. A (end of Sermo I; Sermo II begins below on the same page). Margins at 'occultorum dispensationis mysteriorum': 'al. occulto dispensationis mysterio' (partly legible); a further small variant near 'in caelo' is illegible. Printed p. 15 line 2 has damaged letters: '[s]uper' and '[i]n quo' supplied from the visible remains. 'adnuntiantes' printed 'adnunciantes'. Luke 2:13-14 behind 'gloriam ... pacem' (no marginal note). The Greek column was not used: OCR damaged.
